bull_case: Nu's moat is widening through primary-bank data, direct deposits, low-cost distribution and AI underwriting. Deeper relationships improve both monetization and credit quality, reinforcing the flywheel.
bear_case: Most products are economically substitutable and customers can multi-bank. Incumbents with large deposit bases can copy digital features, while regulation can constrain data and cross-sell advantages.
thesis: NU's moat is widening, though it is behavioral and data-driven rather than contractual. Customer scale, deposits, credit balances and ARPAC all show sustained growth. Primary-bank customers have better credit outcomes, giving Nu more data and lower risk as engagement deepens. NuFormer extends that loop into underwriting and service. The main limit is easy multi-banking and the ability of incumbents to replicate individual digital products.

evidence.claim: Customers increased from 93.9M in 2023 to 114.2M in 2024, 131.0M in 2025 and 138.9M by Q2 2026.
Deposits grew from $23.7B in 2023 to $28.9B in 2024, $41.9B in 2025 and $45.3B by Q2 2026.
Nu reported leadership in Brazilian primary banking relationships and delinquency around half the portfolio average for PBR customers, indicating engagement improves underwriting data and economics.
NuFormer is in production across Brazil and Mexico card portfolios and Brazil unsecured lending, while AI agents handle more than 60% of Brazil support conversations at or above human parity.

counterevidence: Customers can hold accounts at multiple banks, limiting hard switching costs.
Large banks and fintechs can copy individual features.
Deposit funding can be competed away through pricing.
Credit losses can overwhelm data advantages during stress.
falsifiers: PBR share declines while customer count still grows.
Deposit growth requires structurally uneconomic pricing.
NuFormer fails to improve loss-adjusted returns versus prior underwriting models.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Primary metrics show expanding customer scale, deposits, ARPAC and PBR depth rather than persistent moat erosion.

key_kpis.name: Risk-adjusted credit performance
key_kpis.threshold: data advantage translates into better loss-adjusted returns

subscores.rationale: Primary-bank relationships, rising ARPAC and direct deposits deepen wallet share and behavioral switching friction, though customers can still multi-bank.
Customers, deposits, credit balances and ARPAC provide 3+ primary scale metrics with clear multi-year growth trends. Hard contractual switching-cost evidence is insufficient for 90.
Low-cost distribution, deposits, proprietary data/AI and broad product relationships provide multiple defensive layers against commoditization of individual products.

uncertainties.rationale: The moat depends on relationship depth rather than contractual lock-in.
Multiple same-definition metrics show sustained scale growth.
Well-capitalized incumbents can imitate individual products and compete on deposit pricing.
